summary: The LDAP module is competent at unauth RootDSE recon, anonymous-bind/read, cleartext-389 flagging, and one flavour of authenticated user/computer enumeration (persons + computers-with-delegation, plus the domain object). It is thin everywhere else that the MS-ADTS / RFC 4511-4519 surface actually pays: no group / trust / GPO / OU / schema / site enumeration, no AD-CS (ESC1-8) template reads, no LAPS / gMSA password harvesting, no RBCD detection, no DCSync-right check, no fine-grained password policy, no LDAP signing / channel-binding probe (the module flags cleartext but never actually tests whether a signed bind is *required*), no StartTLS probe on 389, no SASL "ANONYMOUS" / GSSAPI negotiation quirks, and no fanout of the discovered users / hostnames / domain to the shared registries other modules feed from.

missing_capabilities.name: ldap-signing-not-required probe
missing_capabilities.description: Attempt a NTLM SASL bind WITHOUT sign+seal on cleartext 389 and observe whether the DC accepts it. When it does, ntlmrelayx-to-LDAP relay works end-to-end (RBCD, Shadow-Credentials, DCSync grants) - a hard 'high' finding. Currently the module always seals on 389 and only flags cleartext as a general medium; it never proves the enforcement gap.

missing_capabilities.name: LDAP channel-binding (EPA) not enforced probe
missing_capabilities.description: On LDAPS/3269, perform an NTLM SASL bind WITHOUT the tls-server-end-point channel-binding token in the AV_PAIRS of the AUTHENTICATE message and observe acceptance. When accepted, cross-protocol NTLM relay to LDAPS is viable - the whole point of ADV190023 / KB4520412. The wire library is already there (recce/ad/ntlm); the module just never omits CBT to test.

missing_capabilities.name: StartTLS extended-op probe (1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.20037)
missing_capabilities.description: Send an ExtendedRequest for OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.20037 on 389. If StartTLS is unsupported, 389 has no in-band upgrade at all - stronger cleartext finding. If supported, capture the served cert (SAN, notAfter, issuer, self-signed) as the same fingerprint any other TLS probe would.

missing_capabilities.name: SASL mechanism analysis (ANONYMOUS / DIGEST-MD5 / CRAM-MD5 downgrade surface)
missing_capabilities.description: supportedSASLMechanisms is fetched into pr['sasl'] but nothing looks at it. Presence of 'ANONYMOUS' (RFC 4505), 'DIGEST-MD5', 'CRAM-MD5', or 'PLAIN' on a DC indicates a legacy / mis-hardened directory. Also enumerate what is MISSING - a DC without GSSAPI at all is an ADAM/AD LDS non-domain instance.

missing_capabilities.name: SASL ANONYMOUS mechanism bind attempt
missing_capabilities.description: Try SASL 'ANONYMOUS' bind (trace token in credentials) separately from an empty simple bind. Some servers reject empty simple binds but accept SASL ANONYMOUS - a distinct RFC 4505 path.

missing_capabilities.name: Groups enumeration (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, DnsAdmins, Exchange trustees)
missing_capabilities.description: Module enumerates users and computers but never runs (objectCategory=group). Missing the privileged-group memberships needed to build the actual admin roster (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Backup Operators, Server Operators, Account Operators, DnsAdmins, Organization Management). member/memberOf resolution today is truncated to memberOf on the user - loses the reverse direction.

missing_capabilities.name: Nested membership via LDAP_MATCHING_RULE_IN_CHAIN (1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941)
missing_capabilities.description: Effective membership requires (memberOf:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:=<groupDN>) to walk the group graph transitively - the standard AD trick for finding all effective Domain Admins including nested ones. Not used anywhere.

missing_capabilities.name: Trusts enumeration (trustedDomain objects)
missing_capabilities.description: Search System container for (objectClass=trustedDomain) to read trustPartner, trustDirection, trustAttributes, trustType, flatName, securityIdentifier. Trusts with SID-history-not-filtered (trustAttributes & QUARANTINED_DOMAIN = 0) or FOREST_TRANSITIVE across weak boundaries are prime lateral-movement pivots (foreign-security-principal abuse).

missing_capabilities.name: GPO enumeration + SYSVOL cpassword pointer
missing_capabilities.description: Search (objectClass=groupPolicyContainer) for cn/displayName/gPCFileSysPath. Each gPCFileSysPath is a UNC to \\domain\SYSVOL\...\Policies\{GUID}\ where Groups.xml / Services.xml historically held MS14-025 cpassword blobs. The module never lists GPOs, so downstream SMB module has no map to walk.

missing_capabilities.name: AD-CS enrollment services + certificate templates (ESC1-ESC8 preconditions)
missing_capabilities.description: Read CN=Configuration,DC=...,CN=Services,CN=Public Key Services: (objectClass=pKIEnrollmentService) for CA hosts + (objectClass=pKICertificateTemplate). Templates with msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT + msPKI-Enrollment-Flag lacking PEND_ALL_REQUESTS + Client Authentication EKU + low-priv enroll ACE = ESC1. This is a Certipy-class of finding that the module currently produces zero of.

missing_capabilities.name: LAPS password read (ms-Mcs-AdmPwd, msLAPS-Password, msLAPS-EncryptedPassword)
missing_capabilities.description: For each computer where the bound principal can read ms-Mcs-AdmPwd (legacy) or msLAPS-Password / msLAPS-EncryptedPassword (Windows LAPS), pull it. A single readable value is a local-admin credential fanout - hash-fuel for the shared credential store. The module reads dNSHostName/OS but never asks for LAPS attrs.

missing_capabilities.name: gMSA password blob read (msDS-ManagedPassword on msDS-GroupManagedServiceAccount)
missing_capabilities.description: Search (objectClass=msDS-GroupManagedServiceAccount) with msDS-ManagedPassword and msDS-GroupMSAMembership requested. Any principal in msDS-GroupMSAMembership receives the KDS-blob (MS-GKDI); the NT hash is derived offline - persistent creds for the service. Not attempted.

missing_capabilities.name: RBCD attribute enumeration (msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity)
missing_capabilities.description: The module reads msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo (constrained TO) but never msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity (constrained FROM = RBCD). An RBCD ACL on a computer with an attacker-controlled principal in the security descriptor is one Rubeus s4u away from SYSTEM on that box.

missing_capabilities.name: DCSync right probe (GetChanges + GetChangesAll on domain-DN ACL)
missing_capabilities.description: Read nTSecurityDescriptor of the domain NC and look for the bound principal (or a group they are in) holding the extended-rights GUIDs 1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 (DS-Replication-Get-Changes) and 1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 (DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All). Requires the SACL/DACL SD_FLAGS control (1.2.840.113556.1.4.801) with value 0x7. When present -> secretsdump.py -just-dc-user path.

missing_capabilities.name: Fine-Grained Password Policies (msDS-PasswordSettings / PSO)
missing_capabilities.description: Read CN=Password Settings Container,CN=System,<domainDN> for (objectClass=msDS-PasswordSettings) - each PSO carries msDS-LockoutThreshold, msDS-MinimumPasswordLength, msDS-PasswordSettingsPrecedence and msDS-PSOAppliesTo (principals it targets). A permissive PSO applied to Domain Admins negates a strict domain default entirely.

missing_capabilities.name: AdminSDHolder ACL diff / adminCount=1 stragglers
missing_capabilities.description: adminCount=1 on principals who are no longer members of protected groups (post-SDPROP) is the AdminSDHolder-persistence signature - Mimikatz / SDPropagator abuse leaves it behind. Also read CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,<domainDN>'s nTSecurityDescriptor and diff for non-default trustees.

missing_capabilities.name: Site / subnet / DC topology enumeration (configurationNamingContext)
missing_capabilities.description: Read Sites, Subnets, and Servers under configurationNamingContext to map every DC in the forest, their site, and the subnets that trust them. This produces a full replication topology - the input to picking a DC to relay to / DCSync from, and a superset of what nltest /dclist gives.

missing_capabilities.name: Schema enumeration (schemaNamingContext)
missing_capabilities.description: Read schemaNamingContext for classSchema/attributeSchema entries with lDAPDisplayName - reveals custom attributes (frequently used to store secrets, e.g. 'appPassword', 'apiKey', 'legacyCred'). Also picks up whether ms-Mcs-AdmPwd or msLAPS-* schema extensions are present (LAPS deployed).

missing_capabilities.name: Password-age / stale-account / never-expires triage
missing_capabilities.description: Users are enumerated but pwdLastSet, lastLogonTimestamp, badPwdCount, and DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD (0x10000) are not surfaced. Accounts with pwdLastSet older than the domain maxPwdAge (or > 5y) or DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD set are password-spray gold; badPwdCount != 0 indicates prior spray. Cheap to add - attrs are already in the paged rows we would ask for.

missing_capabilities.name: Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access group check
missing_capabilities.description: Membership of well-known SID S-1-5-32-554 (Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access) containing 'Anonymous' or 'Authenticated Users' downgrades LDAP anonymous read semantics to the Windows 2000 model - explains a lot of otherwise-inexplicable anon reads and is a legacy footgun.

missing_capabilities.name: Kerberos-only accounts / DES-only accounts (msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes)
missing_capabilities.description: msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 0x1|0x2 (DES) or missing AES bits on a service account = weak Kerberoast crackable in seconds and RC4 downgrade surface. Not surfaced.

missing_capabilities.name: MS-ADTS SPN duplicates / SPN-on-user-with-weak-pw kerberoast target quality
missing_capabilities.description: The module lists SPNs on users but doesn't score them - accounts with SPN AND (DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD OR pwdLastSet very old OR RC4-only etypes) are 'high-value kerberoast' - the target picker for the offline crack. Score and rank rather than dumping the flat list.

missing_capabilities.name: Foreign Security Principal enumeration (cross-domain SID history)
missing_capabilities.description: CN=ForeignSecurityPrincipals,<domainDN>: principals from other domains/forests referenced locally. Paired with the trust enumeration above, reveals cross-forest attack pivots and SID-history abuse (Kerberos golden-ticket cross-forest).

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2021-42278 / CVE-2021-42287 (sAMAccountName spoofing / noPac) patch signal
missing_capabilities.description: Correlate operatingSystemVersion / operatingSystemHotfix on DC computer objects against the November-2021 patch baseline. Unpatched DCs are the noPac / sAMAccountName-spoofing target. Data already retrievable via LDAP; not correlated today.

missing_capabilities.name: MS-ADTS DirSync / Repl metadata attempt (CVE-2022-26923 style Certifried adjuncts)
missing_capabilities.description: Request DirSync control (1.2.840.113556.1.4.841) with LDAP_DIRSYNC_OBJECT_SECURITY = 0x1 - normally requires DS-Replication-Get-Changes; server response 'success' quietly is another DCSync-right signal orthogonal to the ACL read.

missing_capabilities.name: Anonymous OtherWellKnownObjects/DomainDNS SD read on non-AD LDAP (389DS / OpenLDAP / eDirectory)
missing_capabilities.description: Module is entirely AD-centric. supportedCapabilities OIDs distinguish AD (1.2.840.113556.1.4.800/1791/1935/2080/2237) from 389-DS (2.16.840.1.113730.3.4.9 VLV) / OpenLDAP (1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.*). Non-AD directories have their own anonymous ACIs (aci: allow(read) userdn='ldap:///anyone') that this module never exercises.

missing_capabilities.name: PagedResults refusal / MaxPageSize sniff
missing_capabilities.description: If a directory refuses SimplePagedResults (control unsupported) the enum currently silently gets the first N objects. Detect and report - and switch to VLV (Virtual List View 2.16.840.1.113730.3.4.9) when advertised.

missing_capabilities.name: LDAP referrals (SearchResRef 0x73) follow / disclosure
missing_capabilities.description: The reader ignores searchResRef PDUs (tag 0x73). Referrals leak internal LDAP URLs (ldap://internal.dc.corp:389/...) - a routable-hostname disclosure. At minimum log them; ideally follow when in-scope.

missing_capabilities.name: LDAP injection surface / relative-DN escape (self-defense of the builder)
missing_capabilities.description: f_equal() takes raw str values and BER-encodes without RFC 4515 metacharacter validation. Not exploitable server-side (BER not text) but the credfree_runbook echoes attacker-controlled server strings into an ldapsearch string filter - a text LDAP filter injection primitive when pasted. Should escape * ( ) \ NUL per RFC 4515 3.

cross_service_wire_gaps: Enumerated sAMAccountName / userPrincipalName list is not pushed into the shared known_users registry that spray, SMB, SSH, WinRM, MSSQL, and Kerberos AS-REP roasting modules consume - each currently either re-enumerates or works from an empty user pool.
dNSHostName on computer objects is not published to the shared hostname/DNS registry - other services never learn the domain-joined FQDN of hosts scanned by IP.
domain and forest DNS names (already captured in probe result) are not fed to a shared 'domains' registry for kerberos/SMB/WinRM modules to auto-scope authentication realms.

servicePrincipalName values embed 'host/foo.corp/', 'MSSQLSvc/db.corp:1433', 'HTTP/web.corp' - these are service+host tuples that should populate the port/service inventory for hosts recce never scanned directly and pre-stage the kerberoast target list.
trustedDomain objects (once enumerated) should register partner-domain names + SIDs into a cross-forest registry used by kerberos/SMB.
gPCFileSysPath from GPO enumeration should hand SYSVOL UNC targets to the SMB module for MS14-025 cpassword hunts.

Cleartext-389 and (once implemented) 'signing-not-required' / 'no-channel-binding' DCs are prime NTLM-relay targets but the module never appends them to the shared relay_targets list that the ntlmrelayx-runbook / coerce chain consumes.
LAPS/gMSA passwords (once read) are hashes/plaintext credentials that should land in the shared credential store keyed by target host - not just narrated in a finding.
Site/subnet map (from configurationNamingContext) should feed the netmap module's known-subnets so recce discovers previously-unseen network segments.
operatingSystem/operatingSystemVersion on computer objects should update host OS fingerprints for hosts recce touched only via LDAP referrals.
priority_gaps: AD-CS templates (ESC1-8) enumeration via pKIEnrollmentService + pKICertificateTemplate - single highest-ROI unauth-to-DA path currently invisible to recce.
LAPS + gMSA password reads (ms-Mcs-AdmPwd / msLAPS-Password / msDS-ManagedPassword) - one authenticated bind can bulk-harvest local-admin creds; module currently ignores the attributes entirely.

DCSync right probe (GetChanges/GetChangesAll ACE via SD_FLAGS control 1.2.840.113556.1.4.801) plus RBCD detection (msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity) - the two escalation primitives every AD engagement checks first, both cheap to add given the existing paged-search plumbing.

LDAP signing / channel-binding enforcement PROBE (send an unsigned NTLM bind on 389 and a no-CBT NTLM bind on 636 and observe acceptance) - upgrades the current generic 'cleartext' medium into a proven ntlmrelayx-to-LDAP high, which is the actual finding operators care about post-ADV190023.

Group + trust + GPO enumeration - without groups the module cannot say who is actually a Domain Admin, without trusts it cannot see cross-forest pivots, and without GPOs the downstream SMB SYSVOL sweep has no map.
notes: Module is well-engineered on the wire (hand-rolled BER, sign+seal wrap, paged results, ldap3 fallback) but the enumeration semantics stop at Users+Computers+DomainObject - roughly the 2015 kerberoast toolset. The 2020-2024 AD-attack canon (ADCS, LAPS, gMSA, RBCD, DCSync-ACL, channel-binding enforcement) is entirely absent. No tests/*ldap* file exists; LDAP behaviour is only asserted incidentally via test_ad_fp_fixes.py, test_pipeline_ad.py, test_credentialed_ad_integration.py and test_hostile_server_fidelity.py - meaning any new capability added here has room to be TDD'd against a fresh tests/test_ldap.py without disturbing existing fixtures.
